releases.displayName: Visional Wheel S5: Dissonant Resonance Game Mode Adjustments and FAQ

items.text: Dear Metas,

Since Visional Wheel S5: Dissonant Resonance launched, we've received many feedback from Metas. After internal discussion, we've compiled the following responses and adjustments for the issues that have drawn the most attention recently.
Q1: Dissonant Dust is capped at just 40k a week, and after that, gains drop by 95%. How is that supposed to be enough?

A1: Based on player feedback and live data monitoring, we found that the original 95% reduction was indeed too high. We'll adjust the Dissonant Dust reduction rules on November 20 (PT). The penalty on Dissonant Dust gains after reaching the weekly cap will be reduced from 95% to 60%.
After the adjustment, any Dissonant Dust gained beyond 40,000 a week will be worth 40% of the normal amount.
For example, after reaching the weekly cap, gaining 100 Dissonant Dust used to give you only 5. After this adjustment, you'll receive 40 Dissonant Dust.

At the same time, to avoid making the game too much of a grind after this change, we're also adjusting the reward rules for The Echo War. Basic and Hard difficulties will now share the same weekly limit of 80 dungeon reward claims. Once you reach that limit, you can still take part in the dungeon, but you won't be able to open Reward Crates to claim rewards.
This limit resets every Monday at 6:00 AM (server time).

Please note: this rule will take effect once the November 20 (PT) fix patch is released. From then until the next weekly reset (6:00 AM next Monday), Metas will still have 80 dungeon reward claims. After that, reward claims will reset according to the Monday 6:00 AM schedule.
Q2: Why does the new Vision add dungeons that force you to team up, and why are some weapons clearly stronger than others, which makes the experience feel so unbalanced?
A2: We understand your concerns about the teaming requirement in The Echo War and the atmosphere around weapon choice.

This mode is a team-based dungeon challenge. The intent is for Metas to team up with friends or other players, divide up roles, and take down the boss together, with the hope of delivering the experience and sense of achievement that comes from a coordinated kill. The dungeon format is there to keep the experience complete and immersive.
However, since it went live, we've seen the following issues affecting the experience:

1. With items and gear BD fully utilized, SN700 - Finale is too strong, allowing some players to kill The Echo boss very quickly. After investigating, we found this was caused by The Echo's damage reduction phase being skipped incorrectly. We're urgently fixing the bug and expect the fix to go live on November 23 (PT).

2. The Echo War only opens for a limited time. Before, there was no cap on reward claims, so the faster a team cleared it, the more Vision rewards it could earn over the same period, which led to unfairness in rewards. To fix this, we're adding a weekly cap on The Echo War dungeon reward claims.

Right now, a few weapons see far more use than others, which affects the atmosphere around teaming up. At its core, this has to do with weapon balance and how effective those weapons are in actual combat. We'll keep a close eye on how each weapon performs in gameplay and keep pushing balance changes, so more weapons and playstyles are worth using.
Q3: Shouldn't the Echo War boss in the Isles of Abyss scenario have its stats toned down a bit? There's no Cradle there, but it's just as strong as in other scenarios. Isn't that a bit unreasonable?
A3: We're aware of the feedback about the strength of the Echo War boss in the Isles of Abyss scenario.

Because the Isles of Abyss scenario has no Cradle system, the current boss stats aren't well suited to that environment. This was our oversight — we didn't take enough into account when designing the gameplay and tuning the stats. We sincerely apologize for the extra pressure this has put on the challenge.

We're currently adjusting the Echo War boss stats specifically for the Isles of Abyss scenario, so it better match the actual combat conditions. Please keep an eye on upcoming fix announcements for the exact timing.
Q4: Isn't the Resonance Box drop rate way too low?
A4: We'll increase the drop rate for Resonance Box once the November 20 (PT) fix patch goes live.
Q5: Why can't I just challenge The Echo again in the new Vision? Do I really have to leave and re-enter?

A5: We've received the feedback that The Echo can't be challenged again right after a fight ends, and that leaving and re-entering is the only way to retry. The request is now on our development schedule, and work on the feature will follow. Once we have a launch date, we'll let Metas know right away.
Q6: Why doesn't Calamity Owl spawn in Isles of Abyss Vision worlds, and why don't ore and other gatherables respawn there either?

A6. Calamity Owl doesn't spawn in some regions of Vision worlds. This is by design under the current rules: when you are in a Vision world, if a land-based Calamity Owl region overlaps with a Vision gameplay area, that area won't spawn Calamity Owl. This preserves the integrity and stability of both the Calamity Owl gameplay and Vision experiences.
If Metas want the complete Calamity Owl gameplay experience for all regions, we recommend challenging it in a normal World.
Ore and other gatherables haven't been respawning properly in Isles of Abyss Vision worlds. This will be fixed on November 20 (PT). Once the fix is in, gatherables there will respawn normally again.
Q7: Is it a bug that the Silent Statue I just got in the Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve scenario has no skill?

A7: We've confirmed that the Silent Statue Deviation obtained in the Deviation: Survive, Capture, Preserve scenario has a skill configuration issue. We expect to fix it on November 23 (PT). Once the fix is in, we'll recall the affected Silent Statues obtained in this scenario and reissue them, which is expected to take 3 business days.

We'll keep tracking feedback from Metas and, guided by the feedback and our data monitoring, keep fixing bugs and improving the experience. We hope to keep hearing from everyone through the Feedback Platform (Once Human Feedback Platform) so we can do better.
Once Human Development Team

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/46276966/09d5d025427bf78c209eeb19f6856fd4ad707706.png"]
Hello everyone,
Today we’re sharing the changelog for a major Train Sim World 7 update, arriving on Monday, November 23rd!

This update introduces the much-requested Dark Mode UI. We’ve heard your feedback loud and clear and are excited to bring this feature to all the dark mode fans out there. Once you’ve installed the update and restarted the game, a pop-up notification will give you the option to switch to Dark Mode. If you missed it, you can also find the option under ‘General’ in the Settings menu.

The Bakerloo Line is getting a spruce up as well, with a new playable Class 710 service for owners of the Suffragette Line, portals to enable Route Hopping with Overground services, updated scenery, and the track electrification has changed from 630V to 750V, allowing third-rail EMUs to be driveable on the route (plus many more changes).
On top of that, this update brings improvements to controller camera speeds and diagonal movement, various Quality of Life changes, performance optimisations, and much more!

And we’re not done yet! Work is already underway on our next update, which we’re hoping to bring you this December. We have a fix in testing which is showing really encouraging signs of eradicating the majority of blurry textures, and we want to get that in your hands before Christmas.
Thank you for your continued support and for sharing feedback. You’re helping us make this the best TSW yet.

The patch will be live from November 23rd at 9 am UTC/10 am BST. Please note that updates typically load quickly, but in some cases may take up to 24 hours to release across each platform. Some platforms might also update automatically in Standby Mode, without your knowledge.

releases.displayName: MEGA UPDATE: New Weaver Terror, Arctic Returns to Legacy & Free Terror Unlocks!

items.text: Subjects,

This update introduces The Weaver Terror, brings Arctic to Legacy, and lets you take a closer look at your fellow Subjects with Player Profiles. We’re also introducing Favour, updating localisation, and bringing improvements across communication, menus and gameplay.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43698514/8222192350c61c0f9b75991afef970e77e50799f.gif"]

Turn escape routes into traps and drag stragglers back into reach. The Weaver (a.k.a the Spider) is a hunter built around controlling movement: slow Subjects with your web ball, catch them with your hook, and pull them into a deadly embrace.
Catch a nearby Subject and hold them in a spinning silk wrap. While trapped, their Sanity drains, bringing them closer to execution.

Fire a glob of silk that slows a Subject on a direct hit. If it strikes a floor or wall, it leaves a web patch that slows any Subject touching it, making doorways, narrow corridors and escape routes ideal places to set a trap.

You can maintain up to three web patches at once. Placing another replaces the oldest. Subjects crossing a floor web are also revealed to the Terrors for three seconds, helping you track their next move.
Launch a silk hook to catch a Subject and reel them towards you. You use the ability to pull yourself towards walls helping you move across the map.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43698514/ab878a41aaa6164672c6d452d37b1f834d1e7e79.gif"]
Introducing Favour! A new currency earned through play and spent on eligible Store items, including roles and cosmetics. Most notably, this gives players the option to unlock Terrors for free.
We hope you enjoy this long-requested feature!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43698514/e34931811b4c3eeb4553a18ce5702ca6e36eab8e.gif"]
Return to the frozen research facility in Legacy.
Arctic brings back the original map’s layout and familiar progression: complete objectives, gather equipment, survive the darkness and collect the fuses needed to push towards escape.
Updated lighting, reflections, environmental audio and frost effects bring the facility into Deceit 2. Watch the corridors, remember your routes, and be careful who follows you through the next door.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43698514/89531f3febbd44a106473def4102ccd269f0b9f2.gif"]
With the arrival of Arctic, we’ve given each Terror the ability to jump in Legacy, allowing you to jump through windows and hop over gaps.
But that is not all, a familiar blade returns! The original Deceit combat knife is now the default melee weapon in Legacy, bringing a classic look to your close encounters.
A long-standing community request has been fulfilled! You can now view other players’ profiles.

Open them directly from your friends list, player options, leaderboards and the end-of-game scoreboard. Browse their accolades, collection, recent matches, team wins and ranked history, depending on their privacy settings.
Your own profile lets you showcase three accolades, display your title and emblem, and track your progression. Choose whether to share it with everyone, friends only, or keep it private.
Keep track of your earnings and purchases with the new Currency History screen, accessible from the Store.
Browse your Shillings, Gems and Favour activity, filter earnings and spending, and expand individual transactions for more details.
We’ve expanded language support and improved how translated text appears throughout the game.
Arabic receives improved font support and right-to-left layouts, including directional icons and interface alignment. Arabic is also available as a matchmaking language.
The introductory video now includes subtitles in Arabic, German, Spanish, French, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Brazilian Portuguese and Thai.

releases.displayName: The Dawn’s Children are ready to fight! New features of the November update

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/ece63186d3c7e93354e33a6979e07a76d1014076.png"]
Hello, survivors! We’re almost done reviewing the new parts of the Dawn’s Children. The third developer blog entry is about the legendary light cabin and laser shotgun. Let’s dive in!

We remind you that all the new features described in the “Developer blog” are not final and may be changed before they are introduced into the game or may not make it into the game at all. This also applies to all visual materials.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/9db06a5d41e83cc1d3e2b4e28f41a2d5de9fd0ea.jpg"]
The “Geryon” has a truly unique feature that makes it a highly efficient weapon in almost any situation: a personal protective field! Let’s take a closer look.

As the successor to the “Gravastar”, it faithfully serves as a laser shotgun, just like its predecessor, but its personal protective field allows you to fight more boldly. Even when the weapon’s durability runs out, don’t even think about running away! Finish off the enemy instead, because the “Geryon” heats up enemy parts when the protective field is destroyed. The heating effect, however, only lasts for the next few shots, so don’t miss: the field doesn’t regenerate quickly.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/b06c1e7cb477eb050051676aa8f1e274cdcf81e5.jpg"]

The Dawn’s Children have clearly found some books on Greek mythology, and they must have enjoyed them. “Persephone” is a good choice for wizards those who like to deal damage using heating and freezing effects.

The main feature of the cabin is that it adds a certain percentage to the heating and freezing effects of equipped weapons, provided their projectiles possess these effects. If you activate the bonus, this boost will temporarily increase even further, and the weapon will begin to deal more damage to the enemy’s heated and frozen parts.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/db99183260a43f722116a7037751a2c174a5120e.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/26076615/81cba9a06565d7dfcff30df2856b94f4b51d1833.jpg"]
The next update will also bring many other changes.

Remember the “Short circuit” brawl? The mode has been reworked, and now you’ll have the chance to temporarily try it out in arcade PvP missions. A new mode inspired by the popular “flag capture” mechanic will also be making its way into the brawls of the new season. There are two bases and two trophies (survivors love stealing resources from each other); defend your team’s trophy and try to deliver the enemy’s back to your base. Classic.

In addition, the update will also include a number of other changes and improvements, as well as fixes for known bugs and the release of previously announced balance changes. You can also expect minor QoL changes to the “Storage” and “Workbenches” interface tabs, among others.

This entry completes our series of blog posts about the new season, and you can learn all about the new rewards and features during our traditional livestream, which will take place next week. Stay tuned for updates, and good luck in battles!

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/11814497/6ffec4cd8b855e5c3c4de5dfef802bd0e8cbebd1.png"]

Coming away from the 10.3.0 PTB, we saw how much of a blast you had testing out (and coming face-to-face with) The Terrifier's Bag of Toys! With the release of 10.3.0 right around the corner, we wanted to give you a sneak peek at the Killer Power and addon changes you can expect to see.
The Terrifier – Killer Power
Starting off, we’ve made a handful of adjustments to some of The Terrifier’s Toys:
Bike Horn: We’ve increased the detection radius of the Horn as we noticed that some players found it difficult to aim at long range.

Acid Bottle: The Acid Bottle was a little too effective while looping, so we toned down how quickly it could be thrown, while increasing the duration of Acid Pools to keep the focus on more thoughtful and strategic ricochets and setups.
Handgun: We’ve increased movement speed while aiming the Handgun, making aiming feel slightly more forgiving, while still limiting its effectiveness in loops.

On top of these changes, we've also increased the duration of Torture, and have made it so that downing a Tortured Survivor with a Toy maxed out on Deadliness now inflicts the Terrified state. This gives the Killer more time to plan out their plays and keeps Toy progression consistent, so it's not harder to gain Deadliness when using maxed Toys.
The Terrifier - Addons

notes.title: We've also adjusted a handful of his addons

items.text: Brooke's Pustule: You can expect to see a full rework of Brooke’s Pustule, as we felt its effect wasn’t satisfying enough. We've shifted the focus towards improving the Acid Pool’s hit potential to make the Bottle feel more rewarding to use.

Duct Tape and Explosive Gift: These have both received small number nerfs as we found their PTB states to have potential to be too oppressive, especially as we make it a little easier to reach max Toy Deadliness.
Jonathan's Skull: We've given this a small number buff to make its effect more noticeable.
As always, we want to thank you all for providing feedback during the PTB, and we hope you’re looking forward to release on November 24th! Keep an eye out for the Patch Notes for all the details.
Until next time…
The Dead by Daylight Team

Patch notes for today's update (20/11/2026), with changes following the taster for our latest DLC, Rides & Relics.

Hello Escapists! It’s been just over two weeks since Escape Academy 2 launched, and we’ve got our first major patch ready to share with you all! Thanks to everyone who gave us feedback on the Steam forums, through Discord, and via email.
In multiplayer mode, both players now get their own pair of spectacles during the night time missions. Now everyone gets to see secrets in the dark. Thanks to everyone who brought this up!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649515/dd2dd162644bbfee34833a3450d540607dcb949b.png"]

The Purfessor and Lockjaw the dog now follow whichever player most recently pet them. We also added the ability to tell them to 'stay'. Some of us think a cat interrupting your puzzles is “accurate simulation”, but we’ve been overruled.

[p align="start"]You can now quit out of a replay via the pause menu. On the replay laptop, you can now view your best grade + best time. And that report card now also captures best time down to milliseconds.
[p align="start"](Shoutout to Steam user Casper as well as our speedrunning community for the suggestions)
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]Everyone at the Academy is feeling a lot more relaxed these days. We adjusted the character rigs and animations so that they’re more natural looking, and a bit less swoll. (Shoutout to review outlet TheGamer for the feedback)
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649515/09f45a1c97bf4a1779f78706ad63a790b22beb44.png"]

[p align="start"]We did a pass clarifying the phrasing of some of the more ambiguous hints in the game. If there are any other hints you still find vague, drop a comment on the Steam forums, and we’ll continue to refine in future passes!
[p align="start"]We also changed the hint scoring rubric: if you ask for the same hint multiple times, it no longer dings your grade. (Shoutout to Steam user Pixel Crypt for the suggestion)
[p align="start"]
[p align="start"]When you hover your cursor over a zipline, the UI now tells you where the zipline goes. (Shoutout to Youtube Channel The Co-op Company for the suggestion)
[p align="start"]

[p align="start"]After heated debate amongst the community, the dev team, and society at large, Coin Crew Games has been forced to acknowledge that the archetypal camel has two humps, not one. So, meet our new and improved TWO HUMPED camel in ‘That Rings A Bell’.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45649515/52081095cde35865d26662d7b68cd3ef9a604400.png"]
[p align="start"]In addition to the above feature adjustments, we fixed a bunch of bugs!
Fixed a bug where books could sometimes disappear from player’s inventories during “Banned Together”
Fixed a similar bug where the theater ticket could disappear during “Chortkoff's Gun”
Fixed a bug where the ladder could become non-interactable during “A Well-Kept Secret”, causing you to get stuck down the well. (This issue was reported to us by Lassie)
Fixed a similar bug where the xylophone could become non-interactive during “Deciphering Melodies”.
Fixed the persistent bug that was causing a purple shadow to appear on flat surfaces.
Fixed an incorrect puzzle orientation in the “Clues and Cubes” quest.
Fixed a bug where guest’s appearance wasn’t properly saving across multiple sessions.

Adjusted colliders in the escape room “Mind Your Elders”, so that you can no longer easily sequence break via parkour. (If you’re really good at parkour, you may still be able to do it, but at that point… you’ve earned it!)
Fixed a bug where after replaying a room, you would sometimes be taken directly into the following room. Now you always returned to your dorm after a replay.
Tweaked a few constellation graphics in ‘That Rings A Bell’ to further differentiate them.
Tweaked the color of the large bell in ‘That Rings A Bell’ to make it stand out better.
Fixed an issue with ‘new dialogue’ pip remaining over some NPCs heads even after talking to them.
Fixed a sequence break during “A Well-Kept Secret” where you could skip the cutscene where Alistair Bell revealed his true identity.
Fixed a bug where talking to Nate Noah Nameson the newspaper editor re-triggered the ‘quest complete' sound.
Made the “Submit” button on 'Breaking Clues’ bigger and clearer.
We no longer allow players to buy items from the store room before they receive the shopping list. This is to prevent a feel-bad moment where players waste money without realizing it.
Make the pressed state of the buttons on the ”Chord”\ puzzle in “Deciphering Melodies” visually clearer.
Fixed an issue where music note labels during “Deciphering Melodies” would sometimes be incorrect after reloading a save.
Adjusted numerous splitscreen cameras for better visibility.
Restored a missing warning sign to a crate in “Unlock and Load”
Fixed several occlusion culling bugs.
Fixed a typo in Reina’s biography.
Fixed an issue where occasionally a quest step wouldn’t get properly checked off in the journal.
Fixed several collision traps and collider sizing issues.

Fixed a bug where exiting the game would overwrite the last manual save slot.
Fixed a bug where you could not play the 'E' note on the accordion in the “Accordion To Plan” quest.

releases.displayName: Third Stability Update for Transport Fever 3 Available Now

items.text: Today, we are happy to release the third stability update for Transport Fever 3, bringing another round of improvements and fixes to the game. This update is being released simultaneously across all platforms, with console players also receiving all relevant improvements and fixes released since launch, including those from the previous two stability updates. Additionally, the mod activation size limit for console players has been extended to be almost twice as big.

We want to thank everyone who has taken the time to share their experiences, report issues and provide feedback. Your continued enthusiasm and discussion mean a great deal to us and help us identify where to focus our attention.

While stability remains a top priority, this update also introduces the first additional usability improvements. We have improved the sorting and display of train and tram configuration in the vehicle store, and simplified the configuration of alternative terminals in the line manager, signals, double-slip switches and railroad crossings. The default graphics settings for Steam Deck users have also been improved.

The mod hub is another area where improvements have been implemented. This update introduces better error handling and clearer error messages when browsing mods, a more informative interface and display of available mod storage space, as well as fixes for various other mod-related issues. Beyond these changes to the mod hub, the update also includes numerous additional fixes and improvements across the game, including refinements to vehicle overtaking and further stability enhancements, to make the overall experience more reliable.
You can find the full release notes here.
If you are experiencing additional issues that are not addressed by this patch, please share them with us using our offical forum.

We are thrilled to see the great interest in Transport Fever 3 and so many players enjoying the game. At the same time, we are very much aware that there are still issues to resolve and aspects of the game that do not yet meet your expectations. We continue to read your feedback, reviews and suggestions carefully. Our work is far from finished, and we remain committed to addressing as many outstanding issues as possible, improving performance, tuning gameplay, and enhancing functionality to make Transport Fever 3 the experience we all want it to be.

Beyond the stability updates already released, we are also working on more significant improvements to the game, and we are planning to release the first broader game update featuring substantial improvements before the end of this year.

We know you are eager to see these improvements arrive, and we share that enthusiasm. The team is working hard to deliver them as quickly as possible, while taking the time to thoroughly test each change and ensure that the updates make the game even more enjoyable.
Thank you for your enthusiasm, honest feedback and, above all, your patience. We truly appreciate your support and look forward to making Transport Fever 3 even better with every update.
The Urban Games Team
Greetings, Queens and Kings,

notes.title: We're continuing to polish and fine-tune The Zibbo Show for you, and this time we've put together a new Hotfix addressing several issues we've identified, covering everything from technical fixes and readability improvements to game balance.

items.text: Many of these changes have also been made thanks to your feedback, which is incredibly helpful in pointing us towards the areas that need a little extra attention and helping us make the overall experience better.
Thank you so much for playing, sharing your thoughts, and helping us make the game better with every update!
New keyboard shortcut: press 'i' to open dice effects info, when available.
New keyboard shortcut: press 's' to skip your turn.
The price increase for the refresh has been changed from 3$ to 2$.
The Psychologist no longer uses the Scattershot Roll card.
Adjustments in the difficulty of the toughest enemies in round 6 and 7.
Added 4 new enemies on infinite mode.
The Even Twins card design has been changed.
A new animation at the start of the round showing the opponent’s dice.
New menu for displaying game information, called ‘Database’. It groups together Dice, Chips and Champions.
A new page providing information on the bosses, called ‘Champions’, featuring relevant details and tips for players.
Now, if a player has The Calculator card enabled, their dice that have already been destroyed at least once will show a new VFX, so you can quickly see which dice will have a x3 because of the card.
Other minor artistic tweaks relating to lighting and texture optimisation.
Added SFX for the new Calculator VFX in the dice.
Adjustments to all the bosses cards SFX.
FIXES
Fixed "Behind the Show" button material in Main Menu.
Fixed a rare bug where the round result didn't match the scores shown on the board, causing some rounds to be lost while winning.
Fixed dice score numbers staying on screen after Eye Candy triggered in a column with paired dice (e.g. a PowerPair seal), including on dice returned to the hand by Quick Cut.

Fixed the score display not updating after Quick Cut (and other chips/cards that remove or change dice outside the scoring phase): bonuses the removed dice gave to other dice are now subtracted immediately instead of on the next placement.

Fixed PairWise, PowerPair and SplitTwins seals not showing the score number on the dice they affect: any dice whose score changes when you place a die now displays its total during the multiplication step and hides it together with the placed dice.
Fixed: with a gamepad, chips destroyed by Board Wipe could still be focused (showing their indicator) even though they could no longer be used.
Fixed: a tie or the Reset All chip reset the number of dice destroyed in the round, so players could miss card unlocks and elimination achievements.
Fixed: the Reset All chip reset the round statistics shown on the win screen (removed dice, consecutive turns, best dice score).
Fixed UI being cut off on the right on screens narrower than 16:9 (16:10 monitors, Steam Deck, etc.).
Fixed the gameplay camera cropping the sides of the scene on those screens. It now shows the same width as on 16:9, with extra space at the top and bottom. 16:9 and wider screens are unchanged.
Fixed game locked when clicking on the pause button on the Zibbo Shop while a fade was in progress.
Fixed "Surrender" button appearing in spin of luck when not usable.
Fixed bug that let you buy and interact with store items while fade was happening after going to the next round.
Fixed "Consecutive turns" count in the win information UI, now it shows the correct number.
Surrendering during a match now counts as a round lost against the current opponent.
Fixed Spin of Luck wins (and some other run/global statistics) being counted multiple times. Because the correct values can't be recovered, your Spin of Luck wins counter has been reset to 0.
Fixed statistics from your last round not being saved when surrendering or when finishing the game without continuing into Infinite Mode.
Fixed small build issues in two infinite mode enemies.
Fixed board tiles occasionally staying stuck in the "destroyed" (X) or hover look, e.g. after hovering a tile while its X effect was fading, or when the placing phase ended with a tile hovered.
A tile's x2/x3 highlight is no longer cleared by the end of a previous "destroyed" effect on that tile.
Card position on enemies presentation fixed so they are grouped together.
Happy update day, Civ fans!

Update 1.5.1 is rolling out now to all platforms! Things are busy at Firaxis HQ as we work on Arc of Tomorrow and Earthrise, and we’re looking forward to testing these major updates with players participating in the upcoming Firaxis Feature Workshop. We’ll have plenty more news to share on that front when we’re ready, but in the meantime, we wanted to deliver an interim update focused on refining and iterating on the existing foundation (after all, you need a sturdy base before you launch into the stars!).

We’re building on our recent Diplomacy focus with Liberation, giving you the power to return conquered Settlements to their original founders. On the UI side, managing your empire gets a big quality-of-life boost with the new Map Search and Unit List panels. We’re also iterating on our recent Earth release with Random Earth - which shuffles Resources, Rivers, and Wonders across the familiar Earth landscape - plus the quirky new Donut Map. And finally, we’ve taken a fresh pass at Great People, removing them from City Production queues entirely so they unlock naturally through civ-specific milestones.
There’s more to discover in the full notes, so read on!

This update will do a reset to disable all active mods. We highly recommend giving our amazing modding community a little time to update their work before toggling things back on manually. Using a mod that's been updated and is stable? You can simply re-enable these mods by navigating to "Add-ons" in the Main Menu. Browse your list of installed mods and toggle on the ones you want to play with.
Update drivers: We recommend ensuring your graphics drivers are up-to-date and to double check our Minimum System Requirements for the best experience.

Backwards compatibility: While we aim to maintain backwards compatibility for existing saves as much as possible, some new abilities or effects may not appear until you start a new game. For the best experience, we recommend starting a new game.

Legacy branch: Are you playing on Steam and want to finish your current save under a previous version? You can do so using our legacy Steam beta branch. To join the legacy branch, right-click Sid Meier's Civilization VII in your Steam library, select Properties, then click over to the Betas tab. From there, select the “legacy” option.
As a reminder, you can visit our tracker to see known issues. If you’re encountering an issue, you can submit a bug report with the team here.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/c20bf98b946789c57a521867668f8ebb158d5c29.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/de3ffcd31b212189bf67ed50af79680dd90b4bf2.png"]
Liberation has officially been added to your Diplomacy toolkit!

When you conquer a Settlement or acquire one through a Peace Deal, you’ll now have a third option alongside Keep or Raze: Liberate. If the Settlement was originally founded by another major civ (other than the one you are currently at war with), you can return it to its original owner, which will also provide you a little diplomatic boost with them.

If the original founder of the Settlement was a City-State that you were once the Suzerain of, you can also Liberate it back into a City-State with you as its Suzerain, reactivating your old bonus. Consequently, when you lose a City-State, you also lose the Suzerain bonus it provided. This includes when it's conquered, incorporated, or otherwise lost. Some bonuses that provide a bonus immediately, like free Units or Techs, are not impacted when you lose a City-State. You won't lose the bonus when the City-State is lost, nor will the effect trigger again on Liberation.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/544e7a200272c300c8860fbaae55a82a8f256424.jpg"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/b91fe37e7e8b70887f5cf2c9a648958d7c0df085.png"]

With Update 1.5.1, we’re continuing our work to make things even clearer for you as you build your empires with a new Unit List and Map Search. Both of these new panels can be accessed from the top of your minimap. For controllers, Unit List is accessed via Radial Menu and Map Search from the top of your minimap.

Let’s start with the Unit List, your one-stop-shop for navigating all of your empire’s Units on the map (especially helpful on those Huge map types!). You can search and sort your Units, see useful details like their health, remaining movement, and Unit Tier, as well as information like time to Reinforce and Commander respawn time. You can also issue a few basic commands directly from the list, including Sleep, Alert, and Upgrade, or select a Unit on the map to access its full range of actions.

Map Search now allows a way to search the visible map and highlight items for information on tiles, Units, Buildings, and more. A second search bar lets you choose what to filter out, so you can narrow search results down further. Additionally, we added a helper interface to show you things you can search for, organized by type. We’ll be continuing to improve and enhance Map Search in future updates, but we definitely wanted to get this first version of it into your hands, so let us know how it feels.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/98ea802b78c7fa59bfbb1f2384c0b685b627d56b.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/6b38d2c6462eccf0c5ff9512c75b73a44fd28b29.png"]
We’re excited to report our map team has been busy with two more map types added in this update: Randomized Earth map and Donut map!

If you’ve been enjoying TSL Earth but want some more variety, Randomized Earth has you covered. The map is similarly generated to resemble our planet, but Resources, Rivers, Wonders and more are all randomly generated, so you never know what kind of experience you’ll get. You can choose to start in your civ’s True Start Location on this map as well, or for an alternate version of history, use the standard spawning rules for a random start. As part of this update, we’ve also added the option for a random start on the TSL Earth map. (We might have also added a couple rare easter eggs to Randomized Earth… can you find them?)

Next up, the Donut map! This was born out of playing around with some of our new maps, particularly maps with a large inland ocean. While it started as a silly experiment, we found it played well and created fun situations (especially in multiplayer!), so we wanted to share the fun outside of the design room.

The Donut map is a Pangaea-style landmass on a square map, so it's a little taller and less wide than our standard maps. There is an internal and external ocean (each with Distant Land islands) that do not normally connect, though some lucky rivers, lakes, and Settlement placements can create water bridges. We hope you find this map well-rounded, and have a hole lot of fun with it.

A small UI improvement to call out here as well: during game creation, map types are now organized into collapsible categories; no more big scrolling list. Share your feedback with us as you try out these new map types, and happy exploring!
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/12c714dca61b1dec9a439909da476690843e95cf.png"]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/af7612db0054887222d31e46cc789d72e2ca3fa2.jpg"]

Previously, Great People were produced just like any other Unit, competing for a spot in your Production queue. In practice, we found that they often fell to the bottom of the priority list, meaning players could miss out on their unique Narrative Events and the impact they bring to the midgame.

With 1.5.1, we wanted to make earning Great People feel like a more natural part of playing each civ, so we've removed them from the production queue altogether! Now, each civ's Great Person Units have unique unlock conditions based on their playstyle. Meet the condition, and you'll automatically receive a Great Person from the available pool.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45050851/12d1fd7ab966e40f218888e6aa317055732e48f3.png"]

For example, playing as the Abbasid? Place a Specialist in an Abbasid Unique Quarter, and you'll be rewarded with a Great Person: the Alim. We've updated all the Great People descriptions so you can find their unique conditions on the game setup screen, loading screen, and in-game details panel.

Dev note: We did three things to improve how we calculate the Game Year you see in the top banner. First, we recalibrated the time between turns for each Age to properly reflect the actual number of turns in an Age. Second, we slowed down time at the end of an Age when a Crisis is occurring to represent the turmoil of this period. And finally, we found a bug in how months are calculated when game turns take less than a year in very contemporary times. items.text: We just released another patch on the Public Beta branch. Here’s what’s changed since Build 2950_10. This update improves co-op cargo handling and docking, adjusts harbour trading, and brings harbourmaster radio calls to the crew aboard your ship.
Harbourmaster radio in co-op. The crew aboard the ship can now hear harbourmaster calls.
Harbour trading. The daily market replenishment rate has been reduced from 25% to 6.25%. Buy and sell prices now vary from day to day, with the chance to buy below or sell above the reference price.
Harbour transfers. Paid transfers show the cost before you confirm. The game explains when there’s no compatible berth for your ship, and failed transfers leave your Credits available.
Fleet controls. You can now switch to an eligible ship you own by clicking its tile in the fleet menu. Crew commands in the radial menu are available while you’re aboard.
Wakes and searchlights. Refined local wakes on selected vessels and adjusted the Bernhard’s searchlight beam and range.
Campaign and rescue. Restored Ingrid’s missing subtitle in Chapter 6. People awaiting rescue are now spaced farther apart, and rescue-event rewards account for how many people you saved.
Cargo handling. Fixed multiplayer bulk piles getting out of sync, shovel targets that could interfere with unloading, and a crash that could occur when closing a bulk hatch screen.

Multiplayer docking and equipment. Fixed issues during docking and towing, including hoses left floating after a service. A hydrant can now only be used by one player at a time. Fixed bridge crew synchronisation and drone flight limits for clients.

Multiplayer scans and sessions. Fixed rescue and inspection scans that could fail to progress for clients. Voice settings are now applied before joining a lobby, and clients see the correct message when the host ends the session.

Radar, saves and controls. Restored the missing bulk carrier radar echo in Free Tugs and corrected radar distance units. Fixed an issue where owned vessels could lose mission associations after loading a save. Switching tablet tabs no longer triggers a save, and leaving a seat no longer waits for the exit animation.

Interface, audio and localisation. The crew recruitment countdown stays visible when the pool is empty. Fixed PlayStation resource prompts after switching ships, kept completed document markers hidden in the inspection tutorial, and added a cancel option to the wardrobe outfit popup. Improved shovel sound over distance, corrected shift result jingles, and updated translations across supported languages.
See you on the horizon,
Your Seafarer Team 🚣

[p align="start"]Update 5 for DOOM: The Dark Ages | Revelations introduces Slaughter Mode; an endless horde survival experience that challenges players to battle through escalating demon encounters across multiple arenas. Complete Rounds, earn Skulls and push deeper into each run as you fight to set a new Personal Best.
[p align="start"]The new mode is available at no additional cost to anyone who owns Revelations, the Premium Edition, or the Premium Upgrade of DOOM: The Dark Ages.
Round-Based Survival: Each round features either a randomized or curated encounter. Clear the arena to be transported to the next battleground, where another challenge awaits

Hey Madden fans!

Welcome back to our Madden NFL 27 Gridiron Notes, your source for all news and updates straight from our developer team. We have a special Title Update in store for you today! We have a lot of information to share with you about Madden Week, new content and fixes, Stadium Updates to support Nike Rivalries, Playbook Updates, X-Factor Shuffling and more.
Madden Week in Madden NFL 27 celebrates the 30 year Anniversary of Madden NFL ’97 through the players, presentation, and legacy connected to the beloved 16-bit version from 1997.
At the center is the All ’97 Team, available to play in Play Now as well as in a Retro-Inspired Showcase where you can take today’s Superstars into a head to head matchup against the All ‘97 Team.
The celebration also reaches Superstar with new Legend-Inspired Archetype templates, alongside ’97-inspired uniforms, stadium presentation, and more.

The All ’97 experience carries the theme from the menus to the field. Madden NFL 27 features All ’97 uniforms and team identity, a dedicated stadium reskin, and matchup presentation inspired by the original game look.

items.text: Hey all!
Sorry if I haven't been around lately; the Montreal International Game Summit, as well as my helping hand on another game (Croak), took a big chunk of my time lately.
So here's a small 3.2.5 update that fixes some reported issues:
Removed VR DLC and included VR support as part of the base game.
Fixed bad reflection and lighting that could occur due to bad positioning and rotation of probes in houses.
Fixed a green tint when lighting a fire, introduced by a corrupted texture.
Fixed visual input changing to keyboard/mouse on Steam Deck while using the on-gamepad trackpad.
Removed a garbage motion blur in the main menu that tanked performance on some PCs.
Rebaked shader compilation. It takes a little bit longer to load the first time, but with fewer hiccups.
Fixed a potential soft lock when starting a game with a legacy save.
More smaller fixes.

Known issue: I know the water is of lesser quality in comparison to the original game. I had to implement it fast, but I'm working on bringing Kona 2 water to Kona 1, which should come as part of a bigger Winter update for both Kona 1 and Kona 2, which will be the last big update for both titles, paving the way for a third installment.
As always, let me know if you run into any issues. I'm monitoring the forums when I can!
Cheers,
Alex.
Hotfix 1.7.1 is now live on all platforms!

This hotfix targets several issues reported by the community, including Community Server visibility, online replication, console stability, vegetation Level of Detail (LOD) improvements and Map Marker List controls, alongside a number of additional bug fixes.
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45748053/ba472acd7a8a1cade81b8bd96645fe4ff9d318b4.png"]
With Hotfix 1.7.1, we are temporarily reducing the number of active Official Servers to give Community Servers greater visibility and priority on the Enlist screen.

The underlying issue stems from a limitation within Epic Online Services, which currently returns a maximum of 200 server search results at a time. When a large number of servers are active, this can prevent some Community Servers from appearing in the Enlist screen.

We've identified a workaround for this limitation that will be implemented in the upcoming Update 2.0. This will allow us to scale the number of Official Servers as needed without negatively impacting the visibility of Community Servers.
In the meantime, once the Hotfix 1.7.1 server changes are fully rolled out, you should see Community Servers appearing more prominently within the Enlist screen.

If you’re still struggling to find your favourite Community Server, we recommend hiding Official Servers using the filter options and adding your preferred Community Servers to Favourites for easier access in the future.
QSSR, an AI-guided upscaling technology from PlayStation and AMD, has now been integrated for PlayStation 5, complementing the existing PSSR support on PlayStation 5 Pro.
QSSR provides significant improvements to both image detail and image stability, helping to deliver an improved overall visual presentation.
QSSR is enabled by default, so players do not need to change any settings to take advantage of the technology.
Below, you can see a short comparison showing the game before and after QSSR is enabled:[dynamiclink href="https://youtu.be/Rq47TR8MlwU"]

We’ve continued to investigate long-standing replication issues that can occasionally affect servers, resulting in problems such as Spawn Points not functioning correctly, elements disappearing from the Tactical Map, or players being unable to enter vehicles.

We know these issues have been a source of frustration for the community, and they have also presented a significant challenge for the development team due to how difficult they have been to consistently reproduce.

We’ve invested in additional tooling to help identify the root causes of these issues and have implemented further fixes in Hotfix 1.7.1, which we believe will address the majority of the most commonly reported cases.

Due to the complexity of these issues, we cannot guarantee that every possible instance has been resolved. We’ll therefore continue monitoring reports closely following the hotfix and investigate any remaining edge cases.
As we continue improving visual fidelity across console platforms, we’ve also been working to better manage the game’s memory usage.
In some scenarios, memory usage could exceed the available limits and result in an ‘Out of Memory’ situation, potentially causing stability issues.
Hotfix 1.7.1 introduces further memory savings designed to reduce the likelihood of these situations occurring.
Additional memory optimisation work is also planned for upcoming updates as we continue improving stability across console platforms.
We’ve continued working on the presentation and optimisation of vegetation across the battlefield.

With Hotfix 1.7.1, we’ve increased the distance at which ‘impostor’ trees are used and improved transitions between different LODs to reduce noticeable visual changes as you move through the environment.
Further vegetation, LOD and visual-quality improvements are already in development for Update 2.0.
Patch 1.7 introduced several changes to the Map Marker List, but we identified two control issues affecting mouse and controller users.
For mouse users, an option could previously only be selected when the text itself was highlighted rather than the entire row.
For controller users, it was possible to lose navigation focus when moving through the Map Marker List using the D-pad.
Both issues have now been resolved.

notes.title: We’ve also addressed a number of additional issues

items.text: The player aiming a Mortar will now receive kill credit alongside the Gunner.
Fixed an issue that could cause stuttering while aiming mounted weapons or when playing as a Tank Gunner.
Fixed isolated cases where a character’s arms could fail to render while driving vehicles or climbing ladders.
Fixed an issue where explosions from weapons and equipment could leave dark square patches instead of displaying the correct damage textures.
Fixed an issue in Domination where Capture Point ownership could display incorrectly at the end of a match.
Fixed an issue where Unit names could be replaced by ‘’ after joining, leaving and then re-joining the same server.
Fixed an issue where the player’s left arm could become distorted when exiting water.
Fixed an issue introduced in Patch 1.7 that could prevent markers from being placed on top of existing markers.
Fixed an issue where Voice Communications could fail to activate correctly for some players during transitions between matches.
Fixed several issues involving dynamic Spawns that could cause players to fall through the ground or become stuck in geometry.
Fixed an issue that could prevent players from leaving an Anti-Aircraft Gun if it had been constructed too close to surrounding geometry.
Various additional stability issues have also been addressed as part of this hotfix.
XBOX Series S Performance
We are aware of an issue introduced in Patch 1.7.1 that may cause some players on Xbox Series S to experience minor performance degradation during particularly intense gameplay.
A fix is already in testing, and we are aiming to deploy a hotfix addressing this issue next week.
We’ll share a further update once the fix is ready to release.
Development is well underway on Update 2.0, our first major update since launch.
Update 2.0 will bring the brand-new Khe Sanh map, an expanded arsenal of weapons, new gameplay features, quality-of-life improvements, and much more.
We’ll have plenty more to share about everything coming with Game Update 2.0 very soon.

New beta patch!

WEAPONS
Boomerang: cooldown halved on every tier (30/28/26/24 -> 15/14/13/12)
Whip and Flail: they now aim at the farthest enemy within reach instead of the: closest one, so a swing sweeps through more enemies.

Crowbar: its damage now scales with Engineering instead of Melee Damage, and it: spawns a Bleeding Turret at the start of every wave on top of its kill counter.: Kill threshold lowered from 18/16/14/12 to 16/14/12/10.
Awl: its dart traps now fire 6/9/12/15 darts depending on the tier, and every tier: poses a trap every 6 seconds (was 12/9/6/3).
Sticky Grenade: damage 8/13/19/31 -> 10/15/20/35, Ranged Damage scaling: 80/100/120/150% -> 100/115/130/150%, and crit damage is back to x2 on every tier.
Sticky Grenade: it now bounces off the arena borders instead of landing and: exploding outside the playable area.

Tumor: copies of the Scared Sausage burn now stack instead of doing nothing, and: copied effects are matched against their source so two different items can no: longer merge into one line.
Mutation: the burn chance effect can still be copied once the global burn chance: reaches 100%, since every copy still adds damage.

items.text: Hey everyone! We're launching FirstLook, a new community platform for Rematch that connects your game account to your Discord and rewards you for being part of the community.
"High Five" Goal Celebration: sign up to FirstLook and link your Steam account
"Bucket Flames" Hat: refer a friend to FirstLook

These items are an appreciation token for helping us test out FirstLook! Once everything's running smoothly, we'll be rolling out bigger rewards (such as Quants, titles, and other cosmetics). For now, support is limited to Steam, but we're working on bringing FirstLook rewards to other platforms! If you're playing on platforms other than Steam, no worries, you can still signup now and be ready for when your platform is supported!
What FirstLook does
Journeys: complete tasks (playing, answering surveys, community events) and earn in-game rewards. New Journeys will show up over time.
Automatic Discord role rewards: some roles on the official Rematch Discord will grant in-game rewards automatically once your accounts are linked.
Surveys: some of our feedback surveys will run through FirstLook, so your answers go straight to the devs, and the rewards straight to your inventory.
FirstLook is still in testing!
We're rolling this out early so we can iron things out as we go. That means:
If a reward doesn't show up right away, don't worry. Nothing is lost, and we'll make sure everyone eligible gets what they earned.

Platform support is currently limited. For the time being, only Steam is supported as far as rewards distribution goes, although you can signup with the other platforms. We're working on bringing support parity across all platforms Rematch is on.
Unfortunately, spots are limited to the first 50,000 players who sign up during the testing phase.
How to join
Go to the sign up page
Sign up with Discord
Link your Steam account to unlock the "High Five" Goal Celebration
Grab your referral link from your dashboard's invite page and share it with a friend. Once they sign-up with it, you unlock the "Bucket Flames" Hat
Rewards arrive in-game within a day.
FAQ
Is it free?
Yes, completely.
I don't play on Steam, can I join?
Platform support is limited to Steam right now. You can still sign-up and be ready for when support for the other platforms comes online!
I completed a Journey but didn't get my item.

FirstLook is still in testing, so delays can happen. Let us know if you're missing any items through our official Discord server via modmail! You can contact Modmail by sending a DM to "Rematch Referee" or using the /modmail command.
Is there a deadline?
No, feel free to join anytime.

releases.displayName: Dev Diary #29: FREE Wolf Update Patch Notes

items.text: Hello everyone! This is a joint Dev Diary by Jordi, QA Specialist and Tom, Lead Designer. Today we’re going to be talking about the Wolf Update which is coming out on February 27th with the Primal Fury content pack. Everything in this update is free, you just need the base game to get it!
In the golem update we added the War Coordination system for vassal cities. In this update we’ve brought similar functionality for coordinating attacks with other rulers in the form of Bounties!

Bounties are Ruler created quests that can be offered in exchange for a reward. Any non-hostile Rulers may choose to accept your Bounty. The Ruler that completes the objective within the given timeframe will receive the reward and complete the Bounty.
Bounties can be made and managed in the Quest Overview.
Bounties can target Cities and Victory structures that are viable for other Rulers and offer a reward for achieving the bounty
Multiple rulers may accept the bounty, but only the Ruler that completes it will receive the reward.
AI Rulers can post Bounties for completion. Accepting these will add them to your Quest Tracker and completing them will see you earn the Reward.
AI Rulers that accept bounties will send messages giving updates on how their attacks are going.

As well as adding new content to the Pantheon system, we’ve done a big pass on the tech, flow and gameplay aspects. The main goal for this update is to make Ascended Rulers feel more special, by granting them a special trait when they complete a realm, and allowing them to keep their racial transformations. We’ve also added logic for an ascended ruler to remember the tomes they collected during the game, so that the AI can pick the same tomes again if it takes control of them!
Ruler Management
Once a custom ruler ascends, they will now be moved into the pantheon and out of the custom rulers list.
A new tab featuring all the pantheon rulers is now visible in faction creation and selection.
Pantheon rulers can now be edited and campaign rulers (when not edited manually) will automatically update to the latest settings.
Removing a pantheon ruler will place it back in the custom rulers list (if it was a custom ruler).
Already ascended rulers can ascend again to update their recorded information and race transformations.

Pantheon Rulers gained from Story Realms now default to act as Rulers and not as recruitable heroes. Only applies to newly ascended campaign rulers, you can always change this setting in the pantheon screen.
A warning has been added when a ruler is worthy to ascend but the maximum rulers in the pantheon has already been reached on finishing a session (already ascended rulers may ascend again however).
Ascension
Added 26 Ascension Traits. One trait can be chosen at the end of a game upon ascensions of a Ruler.
The Traits one can choose from are based on your Affinity and the Tomes chosen during the game.
If you ascend again, you can choose a new trait to replace the original one.
When conquering a Realm your applied Transformations are maintained. Your Ruler will be under the effects of these Transformations when next played by you or an AI.
Ascended Champions gain the choice to not partake in new Transformations cast during a Game.
Dragon Lords will benefit from their Aspect skill, their Transformation remains dormant until the appropriate level has been reached.
When conquering a Realm your researched Tomes will be remembered and when this ruler is next played by an AI that AI Ruler will attempt to research the same Tomes as you originally did.
A new option has been added to Advanced Setup to disable the Ascension mechanics and bonuses during a session.
Prevents rulers from starting with ascension traits, transformations and skills.
Pantheon rulers will not show up as heroes during a session.
On winning the session, your ruler will not ascend.
New Pantheon Content
Added New Pantheon Rewards
Crow Master’s Bow Hero Origin
Druidic Terraformers
Primal Good Banner Icon
Primal Evil Banner Icon
Keeper’s Helmet
Marauder Helmet
6 Mount Visualisations
Lion
Panther
Tiger
Stag
Zebra
Warhound
Added 8 new events for Pantheon Godir that can join the player as heroes.
2 alignment based events
6 affinity based events.
Increased the rarity of Pantheon Hero events, which should increase the chance of a pantheon hero event showing.

When looking at how the hero cap worked, we became unhappy with how it interacted with acquiring new cities. Since getting more cities and getting more heroes were both very strong strategic approaches, having them intrinsically linked by saying that each city grants an extra hero was making the game’s meta very narrow, since simply grabbing as many cities as possible was the only viable approach.

The new system disconnects heroes from cities, allowing you to spend imperium to speed up acquiring more. This means players must choose between using imperium to have lots of cities OR lots of heroes, rather than always getting both.

Alongside these changes comes a new interaction between Heroes that are part of the same Stack. We felt that multi-hero stack armies were undermining the core idea of the game, by reducing the importance of normal units in armies. To try and counter this we’ve added a penalty that stacks the more heroes are within a single army.
The hero cap now increases over time instead of being linked to the number of cities. The first hero cap increase happens in 10 turns, subsequent increases each take 5 turns longer.
The hero cap can be instantly increased in the hero overview screen by spending imperium.
You can no longer recruit heroes beyond the hero cap.
When integrating a free city, their ruler will no longer be given directly, instead their ruler will become recruitable (for free) in the recruitment screen.
Existing save games will automatically upgrade to the new system and set the current cap to either be based on the current turn number or the number of cities the player has (whichever is higher).
Added “Leadership Clash” to all Heroes and Rulers. This will reduce the Morale and XP gain for heroes, if more than one hero is in an army

The base game’s version of Necromancy wasn’t quite where we wanted it to be in terms of player experience. In too many respects it felt like all the other styles of magic, and wasn’t really hitting the goal of making you feel like the master of an ever growing army of the dead.

To address this we’ve been doing some major reworking of the necromancy tomes, giving them a focus of spending souls to directly reanimate the enemies you slay as skeletons under your command. Using an early game piece of research you can start bringing back normal racial units as skeletons, with the type of skeleton you raise based on the unit that you slayed. So instead of just having a bunch of skeletons with pikes, you can now have skeletons with swords and shields, bows and even skeletal mages. Later on you can start raising more powerful creatures as Bone Horrors and Bone Dragons too!
We’ve made a raft of other changes as well to smooth out the experience, and boost the power level of the tomes which many felt were lacking when compared to other tome lines.
General
Lowered soul gain per kill from 2/3/4/5/6 to 1/2/3/4/5.
Soul rewards on kill are now granted during combat, allowing you to spend Souls on spells immediately.
Soulbound now also causes a unit to have a 30% chance to transform into a Decaying Zombie under your control until the end of combat when it dies.
Constructing Skeletons no longer comes with any Necromancy Tome. Instead you can now use the three new Reanimation Skills to raise undead units after combat.
Post Combat Raising

Researching the appropriate Reanimation Skill, allows you to raise fallen units as Undead. After combat you're presented with a list of Units that can be raised, any amount of them can be selected provided you have the Souls. The system uses all units that entered the battle on the Enemy side and have died to determine which units are able to be raised as undead.
This means it does not interfere with the capture or mind control conditions since those units need to stay alive.
This means that units that have been summoned or have routed are not valid.
You buy these units using Souls.
When killing Racial Units of any tier (15 Souls - requires Skeleton Reanimation)
You will always get a Tier 1 skeleton that costs 15 Souls. But depending on what the role was of the unit that is killed, you can raise one of 4 different types of skeletons as follows:
Shield (Shield, Fighter, Hero)
Polearm (Polearm, Shock)
Archer (Ranged, Skirmisher)
Battle Mage (Battle Mage, Support)
When killing non-racial units
Tier 3-4: Tier 3 Bone Horror (50 Souls - requires Bone Horror Reanimation)
Tier 5: Tier 4 Bone Dragon (100 Souls - requires Bone Dragon Reanimation)
Tome Updates
Tome of Necromancy
Now a Tier I Tome
New Skill “Skeleton Reanimation” - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise Tier 1 skeleton units from slain racial units after combat. The unit that you can raise depends on the role it had:
Shield Skeleton (Shield, Fighter, Hero)
Polearm Skeleton (Polearm, Shock)
Archer Skeleton (Ranged, Skirmisher)
Battle Mage Skeleton (Battle Mage, Support)
New Combat Spell “Necrotize”
Target Unit sustains 10 Frost/10 Blight Damage
Target Unit becomes Decaying
Summons a Decaying Zombie under your Control on Unit Death
Necromancer - Now a Tier 2 Support unit instead of T3.
Combat Spell “Rotting Explosion” - Can now also target skeleton units
Unit Enchantment “Necrotic Magic” - Increased upkeep from 2 to 3 Mana
Hero Skill “Unholy Leader” - Now also increases the resistance of Undead units in the army by 1.
The following skills were moved to the Tier II Tome.
Special Province Improvement “Soulwell” - Increased Soulwell Income from 3 to 5
World Map Spell “Soul Collection” - Increased income from 6 to 10
The following skills were moved to the Tome of Souls
World Map Spell “Restore Undead”
World Map Spell “Summon Corrupt Soul”
The following skills were removed
Combat Spell “Raise Zombies”
Tome of Souls
Now a Tier II Tome
New Skill “Bone Horror Reanimation” - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise non-racial T3-4 units as Bone Horrors after combat.
The Bone Horror is now a Tier 3 unit instead of a T2.
The Bone Horror unit no longer transforms into Skeletons on death.
The Bone Horror unit now spawns a Zombie unit when its HP drops under 50%.
Unit Enchantment “Soulbinders” - Increased additional damage against Soulbound units from 10% to 20%.
Hero Skill “Soul Collector” - Increased additional damage against Soulbound units from 10% to 20%.
The following skills were moved from the Tome of Necromancy
World Map Spell “Restore Undead” - Renamed to Restore Undead Army.
World Map Spell “Summon Corrupt Soul”
The following skills were moved to the Tome of Necromancy
Combat Spell “Soul Overflow”
World Map Spell “Soul Collection”
The following skills were removed
Combat Spell “Soul Fire”
Tome of the Great Transformation
New Skill: Bone Dragon Reanimation - Empire Bonus that allows you to raise Bone Dragons from T5 units after combat.
Tome of the Reaper
Unit “Reaper”:
Added the Ethereal Unit Type
Melee Strike
Changed from 20 Physical damage to 10 Physical and 10 Frost damage
Added Piercing - Ignores 50% of the target's Defense
Added Breaching - Ignores 50% of the target’s Resistance
Finger of Death
Changed from a Full action to a Single Action ability
Reduced Range from 4 to 3
The 45 Frost damage from failing to kill now ignores all resistance the target has.
Dark Rites - Now grants the Reaper 1 Strengthened and 10 Hp for each enemy that dies in battle. Doesn’t count Summons, Siegecraft and Towers.
Now displays a property that tells that it has a 5 Soul Upkeep but a -50% Mana and Gold upkeep
Siege Project “Construct Soul Siphons” - Now applies Soulbound to all enemies and deals 3 fortification damage
World Map Spell “Harvest Population” - Increased Soul Income from +10 to +30.
Combat Spell “Mark for Death”
Renamed to “Marked for Death”
Target unit:
Sustains 15 unblocked Physical Damage
Loses 10 Morale
Has a decaying zombie appear adjacent to them
Gains a Debuff called Visions of Death that triggers the above 3 effects at the end of each turn.
Combat Spell “Greater Reanimation”
Reduced the Soul Cost of this spell from 35 Souls to 20.
Revives Undead units with 100% of their Hit Points
Revives non-undead units as Corrupt Souls.
Enemy Undead units and Corrupt Souls gained in combat with this spell can be purchased for Souls at the end of combat if they survive.
Tome of the Eternal Lord:
Unit Enchantment “True Death Magic”
No longer applies Marked for Death
Now grants an ability called ‘Curse of the Reaper’, a Full Action ability which cares about engagement in close combat version of the Finger of Death ability from the Reaper unit.
As well as the above balance changes, we’ve been working hard to bring you a whole host of quality of life changes!
Added Random Realm/Realm Trait Randomization
You can now get the system to generate a randomized realm for you, if you don’t feel like picking out a realm’s traits for yourself.
Added new Free City Upgrades
Free cities will now start making use of tome units in the late game, instead of only culture units. These tome units will also be available to the city’s masters via the rally of lieges!
Added Dismantle Province Operation
It’s now possible to dismantle a city’s provinces, if you want to switch their territory to cover a different area. Only provinces on the edge of a City are eligible for dismantling.
Added Enchantment & Transformation Visual Toggle

We’ve added functionality to the spell book that lets you hide the visual effects of unit enchantments and transformations. This means you can have better control of what your race looks like when you take multiple, overlapping transformations or enchantments. It also means you can take a transformation for its mechanical effect, without needing to have it visually update your forces.
For technical reasons, transformations that give you wings (Angelize and Demonkin) or replace your legs (Naga Transformation) cannot be disabled.
Faction Creation Improvements
We’ve added the option to explicitly specify a name for the faction’s starting city, as well as rewrite the faction’s biography, so you can make a faction more your own.
Also, to reduce some confusion, it is now possible to overwrite an existing faction when you edit it (previously you only had the option to save your edited faction as a new one)
UI Updates

Added brand new Parchment Images, just because they look cool!
And that’s about it for big new things! Obviously we’ve also made a huge assortment of balance changes, bug fixes and general improvements, all of which you can read about in detail:
The Wolf Update will roll out across all platforms on February 27th, along with the brand new Primal Fury content pack!

The Dark Culture has been updated to interact more closely with the existing Hero Systems. The Cult of Tyranny sees domination as the ultimate show of power, oppressing Vassals and exploiting cities. They specialize in debilitating their opponents and grinding down their weakened foes. The Cult of Death is one where sacrifice is the norm and a tool for those in power. Their units gain power from the deaths of both their allies and their enemies, critical strikes coming more steadily as the slaughter continues.

items.text: [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/e04b1812e019f05cc994f8e4c4eb7f5686b46323.png"]
Hello everyone!
Rise from Ruin and the accompanying Scorpion update are coming in less than a week - next Monday, 9th of March! Read the patch notes to find out what is to come:
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43512488/50e2d70ddb5c0f66d97ba5a2b95b9942581aae67.gif"]
Move Speed Normalization

All regular units now share the same number of Move Points on the World Map. This ensures that mixing slower and faster units in a single army no longer reduces the overall travel speed, allowing for higher army diversity and strategy.
All units now have 40 Move Points on the World Map
All Scout Units now have 48 Move Points on the World Map
Added Combat Speed, a new stat that indicates how many hexes per turn a unit can move in Combat.
Changed the rounding on the Combat Speed to Action Point Calculation. In most cases you will now have more action points when moving the same distance in pre-Scorpion.
Associated Updates
Form “Feline” - Now also has Elusive
Form “Lupine” - Now also has Ferocious
Form Trait “Athletics”
Now only increased Combat Speed
Reduced Cost from 2 Points to 1 Point
Form Trait “Mount Masters” - Additional Effect: +5 HP to Mounted units.
Form Trait “Hardy” - Increased HP from +8 to +10
All Non-Flying Exotic Mount Traits - Reduced Cost from 3 to 2
Beast Wrangler Ogre contracts for Land Mounts - Reduced Cost from 1000 Gold and 200 Imperium to 700 Gold and 140 Imperium
Floating and Flying units now spend 6 points per hex traveled instead of 5
Passive Infusion “Fast Movement” - Reduced Infusion Cost from 2 to 1
Passive Infusion “Very Fast Movement” - Reduced Infusion Cost from 3 to 2
Defense/Resistance Update

We’re updating how Defense and Resistance work across all units to bring them back in line with their original design intent. The new system changes how damage reduction is applied, focusing on the source of damage rather than the type of damage dealt. We’re also adding a new Unit Role that deals Magic Damage at Melee range, the Magic Fighter.
The Defense stat now reduces all Damage (including Magic Damage) from Abilities that have Melee or Physical Ranged tags
The Resistance stat now reduces all Damage (including Physical Damage) from Abilities that have the Magic tag and Spells
In the case that an attack would be blocked by both Defense and Resistance, the higher value is chosen.
Renamed Damage Channel Resistance to Damage Channel Protection
Damage Channel Protection is added to Defense or Resistance to determine final Damage Reduction
Added Damage Channel Protection: Physical
Rebalanced the stats of the core unit types - Most units have less resistance than defense, with exceptions for battle mages, support units and ranged units which have more resistance than defense.
Ability descriptors like Magic and Base now have tooltips that explain what they mean
New Unit Role: Magic Fighter
Uses Melee Range attacks that count as Magical called Magic Strike.
Have the Passive “Melee Mage” allowing for Ranged Magic Attacks to be used when engaged
Uses most Battle Mage Unit Enchantments and the defensive or generic Fighter Unit Enchantments.

Experience Update

All units now gain XP automatically each turn, even when not fighting. This means your armies will continue to improve simply by existing and participating in your empire. XP gained from battles has been halved which means Units still get rewarded for combat, but fighting is no longer the only reliable way to level up. With this we’re also bringing back Exalted Ranks. Once a unit reaches its final rank, it can continue leveling up indefinitely.
All Experience values have been multiplied by 10
All Experience gained from Combat has been halved
All Units now have a passive Experience gain of 10 XP per Turn
City Structure “Palisade Walls” - Grants an additional 5 XP per Turn to any of your units stationed in the City.

Each Exalted Rank will grant the unit an extra +10 Max HP.

Capturing a Province from a Hostile Player will immediately Repair the Province.
Ancient Wonders still need to be Captured and Released before being able to annex it.
Buying or Capturing a Special Province Improvement will allow you to choose any valid base Improvement to replace it. SPI’s cannot be transferred or captured.

Added a Color Picker to Faction Creation, accessed from the Custom Color Option in Swatches or by going to the Custom Tab.
Custom Color can be chosen using the Color Space and Hue slider

Certain Hand-crafted regions with specific themes, such as the Sunless and Blessed regions, now only show up in specific Realm Traits, such as Sunless Highlands and Blessed Fields. The only hand-crafted regions that can always show up in a realm are the ones from Giant Kings and the Desert hand-crafted regions from Rise from Ruin.

Added new Misc Trait "Sunless Regions” - Adds several Sunless Regions, the Thorn Heart Landmark and Blood Glass Material to your Realm

The Beginner Realm no longer spawns Umbral infestations to make it easier for the player, as both introduce a level of complexity with the fact that they spread a negative terrain with their infestation domain.

Changed the rebuilding of the borders to only trigger on excavating sectors since this is the only terraforming effect that really changes the height of the map. Optimizing all other instances of terraforming.
Improved the generation of the Umbral Abyss when playing without the underground enabled.
The “Capture and Release Ancient Wonder” action no longer removes a unit’s move points. The units are free to move on while the action is running.
It is now possible to use Force March on individual units of a stack

This is done by first selecting the units of the stack by clicking their portraits and then giving a move order by right clicking the map as usual. After confirming the Force March popup only the selected units will receive the effects.
